title: Proactive decision tree and staged escape doors for experiments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a proactive decision tree and explicit 'escape doors' for A/B and canary experiments to minimize blast radius while enabling faster rollout velocity. The decision tree will standardize metric thresholds, detection windows, escalation paths, and automated actions (pause, rollback, throttle) for staged rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private environments. Deliverables: 1) A decision-tree spec with gates and actions; 2) an instrumentation checklist and alerting recipe for each gate; 3) a small CLI/playbook for on-call to execute manual escape actions; 4) automation hooks for automatic pause/rollback where safe; 5) documented acceptance criteria and experiment milestones for product, eng, and reliability teams.
acceptance_criteria: Decision tree document vetted by Eng, SRE, and Legal with explicit escalation contacts
Three gate levels defined (early-warning, quality-stability, business-SLO) with metric thresholds and detection windows
Instrumentation templates (PromQL/LogQL) and alert runbook published in Console links
Demo rollback automation for a non-critical model variant in staging with test harness
Operational CLI/playbook available in Confluence and referenced from runbooks
Cross-team tabletop run completed and lessons captured
metrics: primary_quality: end-to-end accuracy / NLU regression delta (pct)
business_signal: downstream critical conversion or ingestion metric (e.g., message send rate)
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - Safety smoke: sanity checks on infra, model load success, basic output validity (automated)
Gate 1 - Early warning: short-window drift detection (5-15m) for quality and latency; alerts to experiment owner
Gate 2 - Stability: sustained metric checks over 1-6 hours with stricter thresholds; auto-throttle to reduced weight if breached
Gate 3 - Business-SLO: daily aggregated checks for revenue/usage impact before 100% commit
Escape door actions: automated pause, automated throttle to defined fallback variant, immediate rollback, manual hunker-in with mitigations
instrumentation: Required traces: request id propagation, model variant tag, batch size, seq length
Standard dashboards: experiment overview, per-cohort quality breakdown, latency distribution, cost curve vs token volume
Alert recipes: severity mapping (P0 auto-rollback, P1 notify, P2 monitor), routing to SRE and product on-call
Sampling policy: 100% logs for 1% of requests at full traffic, 100% sampling for all errors during canary
Eval hooks: nightly regression suite run against golden prompt set with automatic metric snapshotting

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive auto-rollback reduces exposure time but risks noisy rollbacks for transient signals; selected approach is multi-window confirmation before automated destructive actions
For Private deployments, automatic rollback will be opt-in and require customer policy alignment; default is to throttle to an M1-compatible fallback
We will prioritize implementing Gate 1 and Gate 2 automation for Hosted first, then extend to Dedicated with ops flags
Plan to reuse existing Console rollout primitives and add explicit 'escape-door' annotations to the experiment config schema
